samples.summary: New CLI can no longer log in to any backend that predates this change (two independent skew breaks)
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:95` now always posts `{ code, codeVerifier }`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:279-283` refuses any callback whose `state` does not echo the nonce. Against a deployed backend without this change: (a) the old guard (pre-change `github-auth.guard.ts`) never records `nonce`, so the callback redirect carries no `state` and the CLI hard-refuses it, and (b) even if it got a code, `packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72` runs `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`, so an old `CliExchangeDto` (which had only `code`) makes the exchange 400 on the extra `codeVerifier`. The CLI ships as its own npm package while backends are self-hosted (`packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md`), so this is a real skew combination. The timeout hint at login.ts:335-341 acknowledges (a) but the flow is a hard break, not a degradation; nothing negotiates capability.

samples.summary: A single fixed-name browser state cookie makes concurrent/retried logins in one browser fail with 401
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:131` writes one cookie named `wafflebase_oauth_state` per authorization request, and `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:174-187` requires the callback's `state` to equal that single value and clears it unconditionally. Any second start (`packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27` clicked in a second tab, or a user retrying) overwrites the value, so the first tab's callback now throws `UnauthorizedException` where it previously completed the login. The same applies to any login that was in flight across a deploy of this change. Fix belongs on the new code (e.g. keep a small set of pending values, or scope the cookie per-attempt).

samples.summary: Top-level design doc still describes the pre-change OAuth contract
samples.evidence: `docs/design/backend.md:103-115` states `GET /auth/github` uses guard `AuthGuard('github')` (it is `GitHubAuthGuard`, auth.controller.ts:95) and describes the callback as unconditionally upserting the user, minting tokens and redirecting to `FRONTEND_URL` — with no mention of the mandatory `state` validation, the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, or the new 401 path. `packages/backend/README.md:184-185,390-392` carries the same stale description. `docs/design/rest-api.md:334,351` and `docs/design/cli.md:168-192` were updated; these were not.

samples.summary: cli.md still documents the single timeout message the CLI no longer always prints
samples.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md:196-197` says "On timeout it prints: 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.'", but `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:335-341` now emits a different message when an unbound code was seen (`sawUnboundCode`).

samples.summary: Sibling commands left inconsistent: `ctx list` (and `status`) still print prose while `ctx switch` was converted to the envelope
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:47` still does `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` for `ctx list`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:8-10` follows the same prose pattern, while `ctx switch` at `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:60-77` was moved to `errorEnvelope(...)` with `command`. An agent parsing stderr line-delimited now gets an envelope from one sibling and prose from the other for the identical failure.

samples.summary: `runCli` registers a `preAction` hook on the program it is handed, so hooks accumulate if a caller reuses a program
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/cli.ts:80-82` calls `program.hook('preAction', ...)` on every invocation. `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` calls it once, but `packages/cli/test/output.test.ts` (runCli entrypoint block) and any embedder that passes its own `Command` and calls `runCli` twice will attach a second hook to the same program each time.

finding.summary: New CLI can no longer log in to any backend that predates this change (two independent skew breaks)
finding.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:95` now always posts `{ code, codeVerifier }`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:279-283` refuses any callback whose `state` does not echo the nonce. Against a deployed backend without this change: (a) the old guard (pre-change `github-auth.guard.ts`) never records `nonce`, so the callback redirect carries no `state` and the CLI hard-refuses it, and (b) even if it got a code, `packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72` runs `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`, so an old `CliExchangeDto` (which had only `code`) makes the exchange 400 on the extra `codeVerifier`. The CLI ships as its own npm package while backends are self-hosted (`packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md`), so this is a real skew combination. The timeout hint at login.ts:335-341 acknowledges (a) but the flow is a hard break, not a degradation; nothing negotiates capability.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists as described (login.ts:95 posts {code, codeVerifier}; login.ts:279-284 refuses a non-matching state; main.ts:65-72 sets whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted), but it is not a blast-radius blocker. Grepping every reference to the changed contract (`/auth/cli/exchange`, `startCallbackServer`) finds only login.ts, its own tests, and the backend endpoint — and the in-repo backend is fully consistent: auth.dto.ts:13-16 marks `codeVerifier` `@IsOptional()` (so forbidNonWhitelisted does not 400 it), github-auth.guard.ts:105-110 stores the nonce, and auth.controller.ts:144-149 echoes it back as `state`. No caller in the repo is left on the old contract. The only "broken consumer" is a hypothetical older deployment of the same backend, and that consumer was explicitly considered, not overlooked: docs/design/cli.md:235-244 states compatibility runs one way and that accepting an unbound code would reintroduce the injection being closed; docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:55-61 and 107-110 carry it as the accepted acceptance criterion. The CLI fails closed with a message naming that exact cause (login.ts:250,331-346) and points at the `--api-key` path, which is really wired (root.ts:65, config.ts:87-101). Whether to add capability negotiation instead of requiring a server upgrade is a spec/architecture tradeoff (design-fit), explicitly outside this lens; claim (b) also never fires independently since the flow terminates at (a) before any exchange.

finding.summary: A single fixed-name browser state cookie makes concurrent/retried logins in one browser fail with 401
finding.evidence: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:131` writes one cookie named `wafflebase_oauth_state` per authorization request, and `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:174-187` requires the callback's `state` to equal that single value and clears it unconditionally. Any second start (`packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27` clicked in a second tab, or a user retrying) overwrites the value, so the first tab's callback now throws `UnauthorizedException` where it previously completed the login. The same applies to any login that was in flight across a deploy of this change. Fix belongs on the new code (e.g. keep a small set of pending values, or scope the cookie per-attempt).

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present and the described race is real, but it is not a blast-radius defect. Grepping every reference to the changed surface (OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE, WEB_STATE_PREFIX, __oauthState) shows the cookie is touched only in github-auth.guard.ts:131 and auth.controller.ts:176-181 plus their specs — no other module reads, writes, or clears it. The sole "other site" the finding cites, packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27, is a static <Link> to /auth/github: it passes no arguments, consumes no return shape, and relies on no prior contract, so it is neither broken nor a bypass — it is the same entry point clicked twice. The other caller, packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:61, takes the mode=cli branch at github-auth.guard.ts:85-113 which uses the store-backed multi-state path and sets no cookie (asserted at github-auth.guard.spec.ts:167-175), so concurrent CLI logins are unaffected. There is no guard bypass (the path fails closed with 401), no unupdated caller, no removed export, and no cross-module invariant violated; the failure is self-healing on retry. The mechanism, evidence, and fix are all inside the new code — the finding itself states "Fix belongs on the new code" — making it a diff-internal design/UX trade-off that this lens explicitly defers ("Logic inside the diff… is the correctness lens"; "A finding you can state without leaving the diff belongs to another lens").
